validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + CLASSIFICATION: real, and correctly classed as a GASCO national-grid GAS TRANSMISSION trunk (not gathering/plant-internal). Three fully independent primary sources agree, none tracing to GEM or to each other: (1) Egyptian Presidency official site (presidency.eg) profile of the project ‘ازدواج خط الجميل-دمياط' (‘doubling/twinning of the Al Gamil-Damietta gas line'), dated May 2018, giving diameter 42 inch, length 50 km, serving Port Said and Damietta governorates, cost 1,089,000,000 EGP, purpose to feed Al-Burullus (El-Borolos) thermal power plant. (2) marefa.org Arabic encyclopedia entry خط أنابيب الجميل-دمياط, itself citing the Egyptian Official Gazette petroleum-ministry land-acquisition decree of Nov 2016 (explicitly ‘قطر 42 بوصة' = diameter 42 inch), World-Bank funding, Petrojet's own project listing (‘AL-GAMIL/DAMIETTA (42"-50 KM)'), and Eni as EPC contractor — gives operator as Egyptian Natural Gas Holding/GASCO, owner as the Egyptian government, construction start 2016, and a turn-by-turn corridor. (3) The primary source behind (2): a World Bank ESIA disclosed via documents1.worldbank.org, title page reading verbatim ‘The Egyptian Natural Gas Company [GASCO] – EG-GIZA North Power Project – Natural Gas Lines to Additional Power Plants in Egypt – El Gamil-Damietta Pipeline – Environmental and Social Impact Assessment, February 2017' — states GASCO is sole implementer/supervisor, gives the identical 50 km turn-by-turn route, and states the project's purpose is ‘to increase the natural gas supply to El-Borolos Power Plant.' This WB doc also situates P6037 in a documented family of 9 sibling GASCO/World-Bank-financed trunk lines that matches several other rows already in the GEM roster (New Capital–Dahshour=P3930, El Wasta–Beni Suef=P3929, Mahmoudia Power Station=P7580, Damanhour, Suez, Sixth of October, Soumid import line) — useful cross-reference, no duplicate/segmentation problem found for P6037 itself. Route detail from (2)/(3): starts at an existing valve room on the Port Fouad–El Tina gas pipeline near Petrobel (Port Said Governorate, i.e. the 'Al Gamil' end used in the pipeline's common name), crosses the Port Said–Damietta road and International Coastal Road, runs parallel to the Coastal Road along the border of Lake Manzala (29 km to that point), then cuts inland past El-Khalifa village and El-Hawarany, crosses the Mansoura–Farskour road and the Nile near El-Bostan water plant, and ties into an EXISTING valve room ('No. 13') on the Idku–Damietta gas pipeline at Kafr El-Battikh, Damietta Governorate — confirms GEM's Location fields (start Port Said / end Damietta governorates) and the 50 km LengthKnown exactly. DUPLICATE check: not the same pipe as P5132/P6036 'Zohr–Al Gamil Pipelines' (those carry Zohr gas OFFSHORE into the Al Gamil landfall, i.e. upstream of and feeding into P6037's start point) nor P6033 'Damietta–SEGAS Pipeline' (12 km spur into the SEGAS LNG plant specifically) nor P3932 'Nooros–Abu Madi–El Gamil' (different corridor/diameter) nor the GulfPub 'Idku-Damietta' (32in/103km) or 'Damietta-Port Said' (32in/112km, operator PetroGas) records — all have materially different lengths/diameters/operators/corridors; no duplicate found. Diameter/length/cost/route/operator all tier=high (3 independent origins). Capacity (750 MMcf/d, GEM's existing value) is plausible for a 42in GASCO trunk but no source found states a specific mmcf/d figure — tier=low, leave unchanged (not contradicted, just unconfirmed). Note: marefa's infobox auto-renders an obviously garbled '5,000 km / 106.68mm(4in)' — a wiki-template unit-conversion artifact (the underlying value is clearly '50 km'/'42 in', both stated correctly in the article's own prose and footnoted Official-Gazette citation); flagging so this artifact is never mistaken for a real conflicting spec. One originally-cited wiki reference (enterprise.press, 2019 Eni/Zohr-Damietta completion story) is now a soft-404 (200 but redirects to the site homepage, no article content) — link rot, not usable as a ref; not needed given the three sources above.

validity.recommendation: Correct Owner1–4 on the Pipeline operators/owners tab. Replace the current 'Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co 48% / Eni SpA 26% / Naturgy 13% / SEGAS 13%' split — which matches the DOWNSTREAM Damietta SEGAS LNG plant's shareholder cap table, not this pipeline — with Owner1 = Egyptian government / Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co. (EGAS) [state asset], 100%; Operator = GASCO (الشركة المصرية القابضة للقاژات). Petrojet and Eni appear only as EPC contractors, not owners.
validity.researcher_notes: All three independent sources used above are explicit and consistent that this is a wholly state-owned GASCO transmission asset: marefa.org's infobox states المالك (owner) = الحكومة المصرية (the Egyptian Government) and المشفّل (operator) = الشركة المصرية القابضة للقاژات الطبيعية (جاسكو) (Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co / GASCO), with پتروجيت and إيني listed only under المقاولين (CONTRACTORS), a separate field from ownership; the World Bank ESIA (SFG1795-V9-EA-P116194) is a GASCO-implemented, World-Bank-financed public infrastructure project with no third-party equity holders mentioned anywhere in its 314-page scope; the Presidency page likewise frames it purely as a state 'national project' (مشروع قومي). By contrast, GEM's current Owner1–4 split (Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co 48% / Eni SpA 26% / Naturgy 13% / SEGAS 13%) is composed of exactly the three companies (EGAS, Eni, Naturgy) that make up the shareholder cap table of the downstream Damietta SEGAS LNG liquefaction plant, plus SEGAS itself listed as a 13% 'owner' (SEGAS is the plant operating company — it cannot sensibly own 13% of itself). Checked current/historical SEGAS LNG ownership independently (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SEGAS_LNG; Eni press releases on the Dec-2020/Mar-2021 Union Fenosa Gas restructuring): pre-2021 SEGAS was owned via Union Fenosa Gas (Eni+Naturgy JV, ~80%) + EGAS (~10%) + EGPC (~10%); post-restructuring Eni 50% / EGAS 40% / EGPC 10%. Same cast of companies (EGAS, Eni, Naturgy) as the erroneous pipeline row, strongly suggesting the LNG plant's cap table was pasted onto this transmission-pipeline row by mistake. This is a genuine attribution error, not a defensible divergence — flagging per standing rule 3 (don't defend wrong findings) rather than silently passing it.

routes.corridor_desc: Sourced turn-by-turn from a World Bank ESIA (SFG1795-V9-EA-P116194, Feb 2017) and matched verbatim by marefa.org's route section: starts at an EXISTING valve room on the Port Fouad–El Tina gas pipeline near Petrobel (Port Said Governorate — this is the 'Al Gamil' end of the common name), crosses the Port Said–Damietta road, runs 3 km west parallel to that road through fine sandy soil; moves SW 2 km to cross the Port Said–Damietta road and the International Coastal Road; then runs west parallel to the International Coastal Road along the border of Lake Manzala (29 km cumulative to this point); continues 1 km west through farmland, then SW parallel to high-voltage transmission towers behind the Ahmad Shulah farm; crosses El-Salam Canal; runs NW again parallel to HV towers past El-Khalifa village (Damietta Governorate); then west to the El-Hawarany area, crossing the Mansoura–Farskour road and the Nile near the El-Bostan water-treatment plant (21 km for this final segment); terminates at an EXISTING valve room ('No. 13') on the Idku–Damietta gas pipeline at Kafr El-Battikh, Damietta Governorate. Total length 50 km, matching GEM's LengthKnown exactly. I was not able to independently source precise GPS coordinates for the intermediate named places (El-Khalifa, El-Hawarany, El-Bostan, Kafr El-Battikh) from a citable map/gazetteer, so those are left as named waypoints with lat/lon = null per the no-fabrication rule; only Damietta city itself (a well-known population center, used here only as a governorate-level anchor, not the true tie-in point) is given coordinates.
routes.researcher_notes: Corridor is unusually well documented for a low-RouteAccuracy row — a full turn-by-turn narrative exists in a primary EIA (roads/canal/village/river crossings named at each leg, cumulative distances given: 29 km + 1 km + 21 km = the sheet's 50 km exactly). Rated suggested_route_accuracy='medium' rather than 'high' because I could not personally source precise lat/lon for most of the named waypoints (would need a human with GIS/gazetteer access to trace the named roads/canal/villages onto an actual line) — the corridor bound itself is tight and well-sourced, but I am not fabricating coordinates I can't verify. A human routes-repo PR could very plausibly reach 'high' by geocoding the named crossings (Port Said–Damietta road, International Coastal Road, Lake Manzala border, El-Salam Canal, El-Khalifa, Mansoura–Farskour road, Nile crossing near El-Bostan, Kafr El-Battikh) directly from the cited WB ESIA's own route maps (figures present in the PDF but not machine-readable as coordinates from this pass).

summary: Confirmed (caveat): P6037 is a real, correctly-classified GASCO gas-transmission trunk (Length=50km, Diameter=42in, SegmentCost=1.089bn EGP, Location all independently corroborated by 3 origins — Egyptian Presidency, marefa.org/Official Gazette, and a World Bank ESIA; no duplicate found vs. roster or GulfPub); one genuine attribution concern staged — Owner1–4 currently mirrors the downstream Damietta SEGAS LNG plant's cap table (EGAS/Eni/Naturgy/SEGAS) rather than GASCO/Egyptian-state ownership of the pipeline itself. Capacity (750 MMcf/d) unconfirmed by any independent source — left as-is, not disproven. Suggested RouteAccuracy: medium (tight, well-sourced turn-by-turn corridor; no fabricated coordinates). Nothing UNRESOLVED requiring escalation.
